title: Shushing Face Emoji 🤫: Secrets, Silence and Mewing
description: 🤫 says “shh”: keep a secret, stay quiet, or silence the doubters. Learn its meaning in texts and sports, the 🤫🧏 mewing meme, and how it differs from 🤐.
summary: 🤫 holds a finger to its lips in the “shh” gesture. It asks someone to keep a secret or stay quiet, hints that the sender knows something they are not telling, and in sports and bragging it means “I silenced the critics.”
meaning: At its most literal, 🤫 is a request: don't tell anyone. It sits next to surprise party plans, early news about a job or pregnancy, and anything prefaced with “between us.” It can also mean actual quiet, as in a text from a library, a cinema or a house with a sleeping baby. In both cases the tone is conspiratorial, not stern.

Often the sender is the one keeping the secret. Replying 🤫 to “where are we going for my birthday?” means “I'm not saying.” Posting it with a blurred photo or a vague caption teases an announcement. This makes it a staple of marketing and of “soft launching” a relationship, where part of the fun is letting people know there is something they do not know.

A more boastful meaning comes from sports. Athletes put a finger to their lips after scoring in front of a hostile crowd, telling the other side to be quiet. Fans and players use 🤫 the same way after a win, and the gesture has spread to anyone proving doubters wrong. It also goes with the phrase “moving in silence,” meaning working hard without announcing it.

Since 2023 it has had a meme role too. The pair 🤫🧏 stands for “mewing,” a tongue-posture trend claimed to sharpen the jawline. The joke is that someone asked a question cannot answer because they are mewing, so they shush and then trace their jaw. Among teenagers, that combo is a playful way to refuse to respond.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It tags information as confidential or teases that a surprise is coming. Between friends, 🤫 after a risky joke means “you didn't hear that from me.” It can also be flirtatious, hinting at something private between two people, as in “our little secret 🤫.”

contexts.label: In sports
contexts.body: After a late winner or an upset, 🤫 floods replies and captions. It is directed at rival fans, pundits and anyone who predicted a loss. Players post it with photos of their celebration. It is trash talk, so expect it to be thrown back the next time results go the other way.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Besides teasers and soft launches, this is where the mewing combo lives, along with “looksmaxxing” humor in general. It also appears with “quiet luxury” and discreet-flex content, where the idea is that real success does not need to be loud.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It is acceptable for harmless surprises, like a farewell card going around or an unannounced team lunch. Do not use it around anything that looks like concealing information, such as numbers, complaints or decisions. A shushing emoji in a written record can be read very badly later.

confusedWith.difference: 🤐 has its mouth zipped shut and describes the sender's own silence: “I won't say a thing” or “I'd better not comment.” 🤫 is directed outward, asking someone else to hush, or teasing that a secret exists.
🤭 covers its mouth with a whole hand to hide a giggle or an oops. 🤫 uses one raised finger and means silence or secrecy. 🤭 reacts to something funny; 🤫 gives an instruction.
🙊 clamps both hands over its mouth, usually after saying too much or to show “I shouldn't have said that.” 🤫 comes before the slip, asking for quiet in advance, and has a cooler, less flustered tone.

avoid: Do not use it to pressure someone into keeping a secret that makes them uncomfortable or puts anyone at risk.
Avoid sending it to a person who is venting or sharing something painful, because it reads as “stop talking.”
Keep it out of work messages about sensitive matters, where it can look like you are covering something up.
design: A yellow face with an index finger held upright against pursed or closed lips. The formal Unicode name describes it as a face with a finger covering closed lips. Vendors differ on the eyes and brows: some look calm, others slightly raised or stern, and the mouth may be a small “o” or hidden entirely. The gesture is unmistakable on all major platforms.

faqs.a: It refers to mewing, a tongue-posture trend linked to jawline “looksmaxxing.” The shush means “I can't talk,” and the second emoji mimics running a finger along the jaw. It is used as a jokey way to ignore or dodge a question.

It depends on the target. Asking a friend to keep a surprise is friendly. Telling someone to be quiet in an argument, or shushing rival fans, is dismissive and meant to be. The emoji carries the same weight the real gesture would.

faqs.q: What does 🤫 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: Usually that something is just between the two of you, which can be flirtatious when it follows a compliment or a private joke. It can also mean they are planning a surprise or simply declining to answer.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🤫 and 🤐?
faqs.a: 🤫 asks for silence or teases a secret; it is active and often playful. 🤐 states that the sender's own lips are sealed, sometimes because they are holding back an opinion. Use 🤫 to say “keep this quiet” and 🤐 to say “I'm saying nothing.”

faqs.q: When was the shushing face emoji added?
faqs.a: 🤫 was added in 2017 along with 🤭, 🤨 and 🤪. Before that, people used 🙊 or 🤐 for secrets, neither of which shows the classic finger-to-lips gesture.
